title: A Hybrid State Space-Attention Architecture for Forecasting the Trajectories of Battery Degradation
abstract: arXiv:2611.19116v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Early-life battery degradation trajectory forecasting aims to predict a battery cell's full state-of-health (SOH) trajectory from its initial charge-discharge cycles, potentially reducing cell qualification and evaluation time from months to days. Despite recent advances, accurate forecasting remains challenging for emerging battery chemistries, data-scarce domains, and cells exhibiting degradation behaviors beyond those observed during training. Existing state-of-the-art approaches increasingly rely on model scaling, large language model-derived aging-condition embeddings, and extensive fold-specific hyperparameter tuning, raising concerns about computational efficiency, reproducibility, and generalization. This work introduces DecayFormer, a compact hybrid state-space and attention architecture designed for early-life degradation trajectory forecasting. DecayFormer combines cycle-level selective recurrence, using a single scalar state
